newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian T-bills to face 35-43 pct profits tax.
newsitem.headline: Russian T-bills to face 35-43 pct profits tax.

text.p: The omission of a word in the final version of a law extending taxes to Russian GKO treasury bills means that investors will face profits tax of between 35 and 43 percent on the securities, a parliamentary official said.

The official, from the State Duma lower house of parliament's budget committee, said profits on OFZ government bonds would also face the tax. Markets had expected a 15 percent tax rate for GKOs and OFZs under the legislation.

Alexander Pochinok, deputy chairman of the Duma's budget committee, said that the word "discount" had been omitted from the final text of the law which has already been signed by President Boris Yeltsin.
As a result, only OFZ coupons would be taxed at the 15 percent rate and GKOs and OFZs would be taxed at normal rates under profits tax, he said.
Profits tax is 43 percent for banks and 35 percent for non-banks.
The head of the Russian Finance Ministry's securities markets department confirmed Pochinok's assessment.
"But there is some hope since the Finance Ministry is working on changing something," said Bella Zlatkis.
The law will come into effect after its publication and will affect T-bills and bonds issued by the Finance Ministry after that date.
The law was passed by the lower and upper houses of parliament on December 25 and 26 and Yeltsin signed it on January 10 and is part of a package of laws designed to raise funds for the 1997 budget.
Profits tax does not currently apply to government securities.
